title: An exception in period three
hook: Compare two highlighted positions in the table.

knows: Elements occupy rows and columns in the periodic table.
doesNotKnow: Aluminium loses a 3p electron while magnesium loses a 3s electron; aluminium’s first ionization energy is lower in this comparison.

misconception: First ionization energy increases without any exceptions across every period.
objective: Compare first ionization energies while recognizing the stated periodic exceptions.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Among neutral, isolated gas-phase atoms of Mg and Al, which has the higher first ionization energy? Mg has the higher first ionization energy. Aluminium loses a 3p electron while magnesium loses a 3s electron; aluminium’s first ionization energy is lower in this comparison. First ionization energy is the energy required to remove the first electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
The displayed table omits transition and inner-transition groups and periods beyond the displayed rows.
Recall: What does first ionization energy measure? First ionization energy is the energy needed to remove the first electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
